explanations: terra: The specified cow is one that does not تثير الأرض, stir the earth; the same ث و ر root and an animal-earth scene reverse the war-horses that actively raise and spread dust.

luna: The source's w-s-ṭ describes cavalry entering the physical center of a gathered crowd; this verse uses the same root for a community characterized as balanced and just, an indirect contrast between occupying a group's center and serving as its ethical middle. | terra: أمة وسطا uses و س ط for a just or exemplary community rather than physical penetration into a crowd's center; the moral middle contrasts with the raid's spatial midst.

luna: The source links 100:8's شديد to an enemy-charge sense, while this verse uses the same sh-d-d root for those whose love of God is stronger; the distinct sense and object of intensity are a specific, if indirect, counterpoint.

luna: The command “do not transgress” (تَعْتَدُوا) uses the aggression root named in the section's gloss of ʿudwān as manifest injustice, and sets a clear limit on fighting even in a military encounter. | terra: The battle command is bounded by ولا تعتدوا; it names transgression with the section's ع د و root and distinguishes fighting aggressors from the raid's “plain injustice.”

luna: Continuing the fighting rules near 2:190, it says that if opponents cease there is to be no aggression (عُدْوَانَ) except against wrongdoers; this gives the section's ʿudwān root a precise boundary in a combat context.
terra: Retaliation is limited to equivalence and فلا عدوان إلا على الظالمين; the same aggression term is restricted by a boundary of justice rather than licensed as an open raid.
terra: A small company defeats a much larger company by God's permission; the gathered crowd's numerical strength is explicitly denied as a guarantee at the point of battle.
terra: When the believers emerge before Goliath and his troops, they pray for patience, firm footing, and victory; conscious formation and readiness oppose the section's sleeping, unarmed target.

luna: This lists adorned horses among coveted worldly goods; it connects the section's cavalry and its surrounding reference to love of wealth with a Qur'anic pairing of horses and material desire, although these horses are prized possessions rather than attackers.

luna: The verse recalls that people were enemies before God joined their hearts; it gives a concrete reversal of the ʿaduww relation that the section defines against friendship. | terra: People who were enemies have their hearts joined and become brothers; divine reconciliation reverses the section's عدو relation before it can harden into assault.
terra: The Prophet goes out early to station believers deliberately at battle positions; the dawn hour is shared, but vigilance and prepared placement reverse the sleeping, unarmed camp.
terra: If the enemy comes من فورهم هذا, in its immediate rush, divine support arrives with marked angels; the ayah answers a sudden charge with equally immediate reinforcement.

luna: At Uhud, the fighting group falters and divides between desire for this world and the Hereafter; this is a battle-context counterpoint to the section's link from a cavalry charge and spoils to intense attachment to worldly “good.” | terra: During battle some believers desire this world and disobey after seeing what they love; the resulting reversal connects martial advance and spoil-desire to the section's transition from raid to intense love of goods.
terra: Some believers turn away on the day التقى الجمعان; the repeated “two hosts met” wording shows a gathered battle collision from the viewpoint of those who flee it.

terra: No prophet may betray entrusted war-gain, and whoever does so brings it on the resurrection day; it carries the section's post-raid plunder into final accountability rather than private taking.
terra: What struck the believers on the day التقى الجمعان occurred by God's permission; the meeting of two gathered forces becomes an occasion of disclosure and judgment.
terra: Allah knows the believers' enemies and is sufficient وليا and نصيرا; enemy and protecting ally occur together, clarifying the relational opposition named in the section.

terra: Those setting out are told to investigate and not treat a peace-greeting person as an enemy out of desire for worldly gain; it directly binds battlefield identification and booty to the section's moral warning about aggression.
terra: Travelers may shorten prayer when fearing that hostile unbelievers will attack them; it states the mobile party's vulnerability that the armed formation in 4:102 is designed to answer.

terra: The enemy wishes believers to become heedless of weapons and baggage so it can fall on them ميلة واحدة, in one assault; this directly explains the tactical advantage of catching the camp unarmed, while the prayer guard provides the defensive reversal.

luna: The verse forbids hostility over being barred from the Sacred Mosque from turning into transgression; it gives a concrete moral boundary for the section's assault-and-injustice reading. | terra: Hatred of a people must not drive believers أن تعتدوا; the ayah directly prevents an enemy relation from turning into the section's morally named aggression.

luna: Even hatred of a people must not lead believers away from justice; this checks the slide from identifying someone as an enemy to treating them unjustly, a distinction raised by the section's ʿaduww/ʿudwān note. | terra: Enmity toward a people must not make believers abandon justice; this supplies the ethical reversal of the section's definition of عدوان as manifest wrongdoing.
terra: The Hour comes بغتة and its deniers immediately bear their burdens in regret; the sudden transition from denial to irreversible reckoning matches the section's preparatory function.
terra: After every gate of plenty is opened and the people rejoice, they are seized بغتة; apparent ease immediately before capture parallels the sleeping camp's false security.

luna: It asks who besides wrongdoers would be destroyed if God's punishment came suddenly or openly; the two modes clarify the section's sudden dawn assault as one form of an openly destructive arrival. | terra: The address asks about punishment arriving بغتة أو جهرة and says only the wrongdoing people are destroyed; it joins surprise arrival to the section's moral concern with injustice.

luna: Destroyed towns are struck at night or while their people sleep at midday; the verse supplies the broader Qur'anic image of punishment reaching a settlement during vulnerable hours. | terra: Divine might comes upon a town بياتا أو هم قائلون, by night or while its people rest at midday; an inhabited place is struck precisely when repose leaves it unready.
terra: When divine might reaches the settlement of 7:4, its only call is an admission of wrongdoing; the ayah contributes the attacked community's cry at the moment of seizure.
terra: Satan and his tribe see human beings from where humans cannot see them; joined to his cavalry in 17:64, this unseen enemy explains the surprise dimension of his assault.
terra: The quake seizes the Thamud and morning finds them collapsed in their dwelling; it is another repeated Quranic formulation of overnight security ending in a ruined morning.
terra: The quake seizes Shuayb's opponents and morning finds them prostrate in their homes, repeating the section's movement from unsuspecting settlement to inescapable dawn aftermath.
terra: After hardship is replaced by ease and the people multiply, judgment takes them بغتة وهم لا يشعرون; growth and security hide the moment of attack.
luna: This asks whether town people feel secure from divine force arriving at night while they sleep; it directly recalls the section's account of attackers timing their approach for an unready camp.

luna: The companion warning asks whether town people feel safe from divine force at midday while playing; it extends the sleeping-at-night warning of 7:97 into a different unguarded hour than the section's dawn.
terra: The Hour is heavy in heavens and earth and لا تأتيكم إلا بغتة; its universal weight and sudden advent articulate the final reality prefigured by the local raid.

luna: The question about spoils and the command to set relations right place the raid's aftermath in a Qur'anic dispute over booty and its allocation. | terra: The question about الأنفال is answered by assigning the spoils to Allah and the Messenger and ordering reconciliation; it supplies the moral disposition of gain after the section's raid and before human division.
terra: The beleaguered believers cry to their Lord for help and receive promised reinforcements; it supplies a Quranic battlefield istighatha corresponding to the camp's “morning!” alarm.
terra: Believers meeting an advancing enemy زحفا are told not to turn their backs; the ayah stages the collision of a massed forward movement with the crowd it reaches.
terra: Retreat from the advancing encounter is permitted only as maneuver or to join another group; it distinguishes tactical movement from panic-flight when the charge arrives.

luna: The verse fixes shares of what was taken as booty (غَنِمْتُمْ); it directly contextualizes the source's lexical note that a naqīʿa is meat taken from plunder before division. | terra: The rule for dividing war-gain is fixed on the day التقى الجمعان, when the two hosts met; it joins the section's gathered battle-crowd to the post-raid division implicit in نقيعة.

luna: Ready horses are kept to deter God's enemy and the community's enemy (عَدُوَّكُمْ); this uses mounted force in the same military scene but as prepared deterrence, a boundary against the surprise assault described here. | terra: Prepared cavalry and عدو الله وعدوكم put horses and the enemy-root together as in the section, while their stated purpose is deterrence, marking a moral boundary against predatory aggression.

luna: After the readiness against enemies in 8:60, this commands accepting an enemy's move toward peace; it supplies an adjacent limit on continuing a mounted attack. | terra: Immediately after the cavalry deterrent of 8:60, the command is to incline to peace if the enemy inclines to it; it fixes the ethical limit separating readiness from aggressive raiding.
terra: Taking captives is subordinated to first establishing decisive control, while the desire for worldly goods is rebuked; this sets an ethical order for the raid's aftermath and plunder.

luna: It permits eating from what was captured as booty (غَنِمْتُمْ); this is a specific food-and-spoils parallel to the source's pre-division slaughter term, though the verse does not itself prescribe that custom.
terra: The command includes siege and waiting at every ambush point; it is a direct Quranic staging of the hidden interception implicit in a raid, within the ayah's treaty-war context.

terra: An enemy who seeks protection must be granted it and conveyed to safety; directly after the ambush command, this ayah fixes a protective boundary that prevents attack on the vulnerable petitioner.
terra: At Hunayn the believers' great numbers do not help, the wide earth constricts, and they turn their backs; a confident جمع-like force discovers that crowd-size offers neither room nor safety.

terra: When the adorned earth's people think they control it, God's command comes by night or day and leaves it harvested; settled confidence is destroyed at an unanticipated hour like the sleeping camp.

terra: When God gathers people, their worldly span seems only an hour of a day and they recognize one another; final gathering and compressed time intensify the section's sudden transition into judgment.
terra: The question asks what the sinners can hasten if punishment comes بياتا أو نهارا; the uncertain night-or-day arrival makes their demand answerable as an unexpected assault.
terra: Pharaoh and his troops pursue across the sea بغيا وعدوا, in oppression and aggression; the chase embodies the section's ع د و sense of an unjust assault and ends in judgment on the attacker.

luna: A cry seizes the wrongdoers and leaves them fallen in their homes by morning; the home-bound victims and morning vocal shock closely parallel the section's vulnerable encampment and alarm cry. | terra: The cry takes the wrongdoers and by morning they lie motionless in their homes; sound, seizure, and the morning condition form a complete divine raid sequence.

luna: Lot's people rush toward him to seize his guests; their bodily rush on a target concretely parallels the source gloss for th-w-r, “people leapt upon him,” and the assault into a crowd. | terra: Lot's people rush toward his house, driven by their prior wrongdoing; the threatening crowd converging on one dwelling supplies the human assault that the dawn judgment will reverse.
luna: The mob states its intent toward Lot's guests, making explicit the predatory purpose behind the rushing crowd in 11:78; this sharpens the section's attack-on-a-community image.

luna: Lot wishes he had strength or a firm support against the rushing crowd; رُكْنٍ شَدِيدٍ uses the source's sh-d-d root for support/strength, not its secondary “charge at an enemy” sense, making a precise reversal of attacker and unprotected target. | terra: Facing the converging mob, Lot wishes for strength or a strong refuge; his confessed lack of defense makes the subsequent night escape and fixed morning blow in 11:81 especially exact to the section's helpless camp.

luna: Lot is told to leave by night because the people's appointed time is morning; this makes the night journey and near dawn arrival a concrete parallel to the section's raid timetable. | terra: The messengers order Lot to travel with his family by night because his people's appointed time is الصبح; night movement and an inescapable dawn appointment reproduce the raid's timing exactly.

luna: This continues the morning appointment in 11:81 with the command arriving and the town overturned; it contributes the execution of the threatened blow, not the timing itself. | terra: This ayah supplies the destructive action when the command arrives and the town is overturned; 11:81 supplies the appointed dawn, so this row is the actual strike following that announced hour.

luna: This completes the Lot destruction begun in 11:82 by identifying its marked stones and saying the punishment is not far from wrongdoers; it adds the judgment's specific target and warning. | terra: Marked stones rain upon the overturned town, and the ayah says such punishment is not far from wrongdoers; it supplies the missiles and continuing reach of the dawn strike announced in 11:81 and begun in 11:82.

luna: The people of Midian are taken by the cry and found fallen in their homes by morning, another specific pairing of sudden vocal punishment with its dawn aftermath. | terra: The cry seizes the wrongdoers while Shuayb and the believers are saved, and morning finds the victims fallen in their homes; the selective rescue sharpens the dawn judgment image.
terra: The promised day is يوم مجموع له الناس, a day for which all people are gathered; it states in final-day terms what the horses' entry into a human جمع prefigures.
terra: The people are asked whether they feel safe from an enveloping punishment or the Hour coming بغتة; an all-surrounding, unperceived arrival matches the charge that ends in the crowd's center.
terra: The people hasten evil before good despite exemplary punishments having passed; their provocative demand repeats the stance answered by the section's dawn-arrival image.
terra: When punishment reaches people, they ask for a short delay; their request comes only after the blow is present, articulating the raid image's lost reaction-time.
terra: Lot is ordered to take his family away during a portion of the night; this is the protective night movement that precedes the victims' cutoff by morning in 15:66.
terra: Lot is told that the last remnant of the people will be cut off مصبحين; the night journey ends in an unavoidable morning destruction just as the raid image requires.
luna: The people of the city arrive at Lot's house rejoicing over his guests; this begins a second account of a crowd converging on a vulnerable household.
luna: Lot calls the crowd's attention to his guests and asks them not to disgrace him; the household under attack is the vulnerable side of the same crowd-convergence scene.
luna: Lot invokes fear of God as the alternative to shaming and assaulting his guests, putting a moral restraint beside the section's root gloss of aggression as injustice.
luna: Lot's visitors ask whether he was not forbidden from receiving people; this exposes the hostile crowd's effort to control and menace those under his protection.

luna: The people are caught by a shout at sunrise; 15:74 completes this same Lot episode with the city overturned and stones, while this row contributes the morning shout. | terra: The destroying cry seizes Lot's people مشرقين, at sunrise, joining the section's first-light assault to the cry heard beside its dust cloud.

luna: After the sunrise shout in 15:73, the city is turned upside down and stones fall; this completes the sudden strike in the cited row's account. | terra: After the cry catches the people at sunrise in 15:73, the city is overturned and struck with stones; this ayah contributes the physical completion of that dawn assault.

luna: The cry catches the people of al-Hijr as they enter morning; its sudden morning seizure directly echoes the section's dawn strike and raised cry. | terra: The Thamud are seized by the cry مصبحين, as morning begins; both the hour and the sound coincide with the section's attack image.
luna: This follows the morning cry in 15:83 by saying that the people of al-Hijr's earnings did not avail them; it states that resources could not protect the struck community.
terra: God's command is declared already arrived and the addressees are told not to hasten it; the grammar collapses their demanded future into an imminent strike.

luna: The preceding question asks whether plotters feel secure from punishment arriving where they do not perceive it; 16:46 adds seizure during activity and no escape, so this row contributes the unexpectedness behind the section's blow. | terra: Plotters are asked whether they feel safe from the earth swallowing them or punishment coming من حيث لا يشعرون; the threat is an assault from an unanticipated direction.

luna: God may seize wrongdoers during their ordinary activity, and they cannot escape; this matches the section's claim that a charge into the gathered crowd leaves no room to flee. | terra: God may seize them in the midst of their movement فما هم بمعجزين; even mobility provides no escape from the unexpected punishment threatened in 16:45.

luna: Satan is told to come against people with “your cavalry and infantry” (بِخَيْلِكَ وَرَجِلِكَ); this is the Qur'an's direct mounted-and-footed assault image corresponding to the section's riders charging a people. | terra: Iblis is told to raise his voice against people and mobilize بخيلك ورجلك, his cavalry and infantry; noise, horses, and an assaulting force meet in one image as they do in the section.
terra: At the latter promise humanity is brought together لفيفا, as a mixed gathered mass; that final heterogeneous crowd corresponds closely to the section's dictionary sense of جمع as mixed people.

terra: The ayah asks whether people take Iblis and his offspring as أولياء although they are عدو to them; it places the section's exact enemy-versus-ally opposition in one sentence and links it to the cavalry commander of 17:64.
terra: The guilty see the Fire, know they will fall into it, and find no way to turn away; this is the judgment counterpart of realizing too late that the charge has closed escape.
terra: People surge into one another like waves, then the trumpet is blown and فجمعناهم جمعا; the crowded collision becomes the final gathering that the section says the raid anticipates.

terra: Moses appoints a known festival day and has the people gathered ضحى, in full forenoon; an announced public confrontation at a gathered crowd is the tactical opposite of a surprise attack at first light.

terra: Moses is commanded to travel with the servants by night and strike a dry path through the sea without fear of pursuit; protective night movement prepares an escape route before the pursuing force arrives.
terra: Pharaoh pursues the night travelers with his troops and the sea overwhelms them; the would-be attackers are overtaken by the medium through which their targets escaped.
terra: The trumpet is blown and the guilty are gathered that day; sound immediately produces the eschatological crowd, as the section's cry and human جمع anticipate.
terra: On the final day الأصوات are hushed before the Merciful and only a whisper is heard; the vast gathered judgment is sonically opposite to the section's raised, sustained cry.
terra: When a town's people sense divine might, إذا هم منها يركضون: they bolt from it; this is the attacked crowd's attempted flight once the inescapable blow is already present.
terra: لا تركضوا orders the fleeing people of 21:12 not to run and to return to their ease and homes; the command closes the escape that their panicked running sought.
terra: The fleeing town acknowledges its wrongdoing and cries woe when the punishment catches it; this is the victims' voiced response after the escape command is closed in 21:13.
terra: Their cry continues until they are made extinguished stubble; it joins sustained sound to the complete aftermath of the divine assault.
terra: The rejecters ask when the promise will occur; it supplies the taunting stance that the sudden, unanswerable arrival in 21:40 overturns.
terra: The promised event comes بغتة, confounds them, and can neither be repelled nor deferred; it states the surprise and absence of reaction-time that make the dawn raid terrifying.

luna: Permission to fight is given to people who are themselves fought because they were wronged; this sharply distinguishes a just defense from the section's morally charged image of aggression. | terra: Permission to fight is given because the recipients have been wronged; it marks defensive redress as the opposite of the section's dictionary definition of aggression as plain injustice.
terra: The wronged have been expelled from their homes without right, and divine repulsion protects places of worship; the attacked settlement is defended rather than treated as lawful raid-prey.
terra: They demand that punishment be hastened, but God's promise will not fail; the ayah holds their impatience against the certainty of the appointed blow.
terra: The unbelievers remain in doubt until the Hour comes بغتة or the punishment of a barren day arrives; the final event retains the section's sudden, terminal timing.
terra: The cry seizes the wrongdoers بالحق and leaves them debris; the section's distressed shout becomes here the just destroying sound that overtakes the attacked community.
terra: When the affluent are seized with punishment, they suddenly cry for help; the distressed sound is the response of a community overtaken by the blow.
terra: The criers of 23:64 are told not to plead that day because no help will come; their alarm continues but cannot open an escape.

terra: The household privacy rule names the time before dawn prayer as one of undress and repose; it only indirectly supports the section's claim that a first-light target is likely unready, so the connection is contextual rather than an attack scene.
terra: At judgment the deeds of the rejecters are made scattered dust; the raid's transient dust becomes a figure for the total dissipation of human achievement on the day it anticipates.

terra: Pharaoh's host pursues Moses' people مشرقين, at sunrise; it stages an army overtaking a vulnerable group at the section's hour, but the apparent dawn attackers will be destroyed rather than victorious.

terra: When the two hosts see one another, Moses' companions say إنا لمدركون, “we are overtaken”; this is the exact no-escape instant of an attacking force reaching the gathered fugitives at sunrise in 26:60.
terra: Moses answers the overtaken crowd's fear in 26:61 with كلا إن معي ربي سيهدين; divine guidance overturns the apparently closed escape at the end of Pharaoh's sunrise pursuit.
terra: The sea is struck and opens into a dry route after the fugitives say they are overtaken; the apparent absence of escape at the sunrise pursuit becomes an actual passage through the barrier.
terra: Pharaoh's pursuing force is drowned after Moses' party is saved; this completes the reversal in which the sunrise attackers, rather than the overtaken crowd, are destroyed.
terra: Punishment comes to them بغتة وهم لا يشعرون; sudden arrival without perception is the tactical essence of the section's first-light attack.
terra: After the sudden seizure in 26:202 they ask whether they can be given respite; their too-late request states the missing reaction-time in the raid image.
terra: The question أفبعذابنا يستعجلون repeats the section's cited challenge, while 26:202-203 already show that the hastened punishment arrives suddenly and permits no delay.

terra: The conspirators swear to attack Salih and his family by night and then deny witnessing it; this is a planned surprise assault on a household and carries the section's explicit moral sense of aggression as injustice.
terra: They plot while Allah counters their plot without their awareness; after the night attack planned in 27:49, the would-be raiders themselves become the unsuspecting side.

terra: The result of the conspirators' plot is their own total destruction with their people; it completes the reversal begun by the planned night assault in 27:49 and the unseen counterplot in 27:50.
terra: The conspirators' houses stand empty because of their wrongdoing; this is the visible settlement-level aftermath of the failed night raid and counterplot narrated in 27:49-51.
terra: Part of what the addressees seek to hasten may already be close behind them; the pursuing proximity gives punishment the spatial feel of a force overtaking its target.
terra: The trumpet terrifies all in heavens and earth and all come to God humbled; a single sound subdues and assembles the entire population.
terra: Those who demand punishment are told it will come بغتة وهم لا يشعرون; the haste motif and surprise strike meet within one ayah.

terra: They again demand punishment be hastened while Hell already encompasses the unbelievers; following the sudden arrival in 29:53, the ayah says the attackers' requested destination already surrounds them.

terra: Earlier peoples أثاروا الأرض, worked or stirred the earth, and built powerfully before their wrongdoing destroyed them; the section's dust-raising root here belongs to civilization later judged, rather than to its attackers.
terra: God sends winds فتثير سحابا, using the section's ث و ر root for a cloud raised and spread across the sky; rain and rejoicing replace the dust and terror of the charge.
terra: The command واغضض من صوتك lowers the voice, directly reversing the source section's secondary dictionary image of a voice raised and continued without break.
terra: Enemy hosts come upon the believers, but God sends a wind and unseen forces against them; it introduces the enclosing assault whose camp-level terror is described in 33:10.

luna: During the Confederates' siege, the enemy comes from above and below and the believers' eyes and hearts react in terror; it reverses the cavalry's role, showing the panic of a beset community. | terra: The confederate forces come from above and below until eyes swerve and hearts reach throats; attack from enclosing directions gives the camp-level experience of a crowd with no open side.
luna: The siege in 33:10 becomes a severe shaking of the believers; this row contributes the inner effect of being pressed by the gathered enemy forces.
terra: The address says flight will not benefit those fleeing death or killing; it supplies a military formulation of the no-escape claim that the section carries into the final day.
terra: When terror overtakes them there is فلا فوت, no escape, and they are seized from a nearby place; proximity and failed flight give the last-day form of a force already inside the camp.

terra: The winds فتثير سحابا, stir up a cloud, using the section's ث و ر root for a rising cloud rather than hoof-dust; the rain revives dead earth and explicitly opens onto resurrection, turning the raid-cloud into life and final rising.
terra: One cry extinguishes the whole community; it is a direct repeated formulation of a single overwhelming sound performing the work of the section's sudden assault.
terra: A single cry seizes the people وهم يخصمون, in the middle of ordinary disputing; the sudden sound catches an occupied community with no warning, like the camp at first light.
terra: After the cry of 36:49 they cannot make a bequest or return to their families; the ayah specifies the total lack of response-time implicit in the section's unarmed morning victims.
terra: One cry is enough and فإذا هم جميع لدينا محضرون: the sound is immediately followed by the whole human gathering before God, combining the section's raised cry, جمع, and last-day culmination.
terra: People pass the ruins of Lot's community مصبحين; the morning hour that once delivered punishment becomes the recurring hour at which its visible aftermath is encountered.

luna: The preceding question asks whether the rejecters are hastening the punishment; 37:177 supplies the bad morning that answers it, linking demanded punishment to its abrupt arrival. | terra: The divine question أفبعذابنا يستعجلون is the exact haste-for-punishment stance that the section makes answerable by the next morning's arrival.

luna: This explicitly names the warned people's “evil morning” when punishment descends on their courtyard, giving the image's dawn raid its Qur'anic counterpart as a sudden punitive arrival at home. | terra: Punishment descends into the warned people's courtyard and their morning is declared evil; this is the section's dawn raid recast directly as divine punishment reaching the camp.
terra: The people await only صيحة واحدة with no interval of recovery; a single unbroken cry and no respite make explicit the section's sustained sound and sudden seizure.

luna: The warning says punishment may arrive suddenly while people do not perceive it; this articulates the section's specific surprise-and-unpreparedness theme in judgment language. | terra: The warning commands response before punishment comes بغتة while people are unaware; the ayah makes readiness the answer to the section's surprise attack.
terra: The trumpet blast fells all in the heavens and earth, and a later blast has them standing and looking; sound alone overtakes and reconstitutes the universal crowd.

luna: The verse says that a person once marked by enmity can become “as a devoted friend” (وَلِيٌّ حَمِيمٌ) when evil is repelled with good; it directly complicates the section's lexical pairing of enemy and friend. | terra: Repelling evil with what is better can make the one between whom there is عداوة become كأنه ولي حميم; it gives the exact enemy-versus-friend opposition in the section's dictionary definition and then overturns it.
terra: Those who disbelieve in the Hour seek to hasten it while believers know it is true; the same haste becomes a marker of blindness to the final event prefigured by the raid.
luna: It locates blame on those who wrong people and transgress in the land without right, closely matching the section's explicit gloss of ʿudwān as plain injustice.
terra: The command urges response before a day from God for which there is no refuge; the lack of ملجإ restates the raid scene's closed exits at eschatological scale.
terra: They await only the Hour أن تأتيهم بغتة وهم لا يشعرون; the final day is explicitly staged as an unperceived sudden arrival.
terra: Close companions become enemies on the final day except the God-conscious; the friend-enemy opposition named by the section is reversed at the very judgment its raid anticipates.

terra: A cloud advancing toward the people's valleys is welcomed as rain but is actually the punishment they sought to hasten; an approaching cloud conceals the blow, as the section's rising dust both reveals and veils the raid.
terra: The misread cloud of 46:24 destroys everything by its Lord's command until only dwellings remain visible; this row contributes the raid-cloud's total, settlement-level aftermath.

luna: The verse describes meeting an enemy in battle, striking, then binding captives; it concretely fits the source's secondary sh-d-d sense of charging an enemy, while its context is open battle rather than a dawn raid. | terra: After battle has subdued the enemy, فشدوا الوثاق commands tightening the captives' bonds; the section's ش د د dictionary sense is the charge upon an enemy, while this Quranic use marks the restrained aftermath of that encounter.
terra: The Hour can come بغتة after its signs have already appeared; visible warning still does not yield reaction-time once the event itself attacks.
terra: Those left behind want to accompany believers when they depart to take spoils; movement toward anticipated gain exposes the acquisitive motive that the section hears after the charge.
terra: The Prophet's companions are أشداء على الكفار and merciful among themselves; the shared ش د د root relocates the section's forceful charge from a momentary attack to a bounded communal stance.
terra: The section explicitly invokes the dictionary action “raising the voice”; لا ترفعوا أصواتكم sets a moral limit on that same action in the Prophet's presence, against the raid's swelling alarm.
terra: The command is to listen for the caller calling from a nearby place; it supplies the close-positioned voice whose cry becomes the Day of Emergence in 50:42.
terra: The day people hear الصيحة بالحق is itself يوم الخروج; the raid's cry is translated directly into the sound that summons the final emergence.

terra: People emerge from the split earth سراعا and the ayah calls this a gathering easy for God; their rapid movement into the final حشر carries the section's rushing force and human crowd into resurrection.
terra: The condemned are told to taste the trial they demanded to be hastened; it is a direct answer to the same impatient stance cited in the section.
terra: The Thamud rebel and the thunderbolt seizes them وهم ينظرون, while they look on; the blow reaches a conscious crowd too suddenly for defense.
terra: After the seizure of 51:44 they can neither stand nor help themselves; the ayah spells out the helplessness produced by the completed strike.
terra: A caller summons people to something terrible; this is the source of the compelled, distressed crowd movement developed in 54:7-8.
terra: The humbled dead emerge from graves like scattered locusts; a dense, disordered multitude replaces the section's mixed camp and prepares the rush toward the caller.
terra: The resurrected hasten toward the caller and call it a difficult day; following the crowd-image of 54:7, this ayah supplies its compelled forward motion and distressed voice.
terra: One cry leaves the Thamud like crushed enclosure-fodder; the attacking sound and ruined communal aftermath repeat the dawn-cry pattern without the morning marker.

luna: In the same Lot episode as 54:38, a stone storm is sent against the people while Lot's family is saved before dawn; it adds the concrete attack and dawn rescue behind the cited morning punishment. | terra: A stone-bearing storm is sent against Lot's people while his family is saved بسحر, before dawn; the same edge of morning separates rescue from the approaching punishment.

luna: The people press Lot for access to his guests and are blinded; this is a specific mob assault on protected visitors, echoing the source's secondary th-w-r sense of people leaping upon a target. | terra: Lot's people try to seize his guests, but their eyes are obliterated before the settled morning punishment of 54:38; the night aggressors are disabled immediately before becoming dawn victims.

luna: The text says punishment “came upon them early in the morning” (بُكْرَةً), using ṣ-b-ḥ, the source section's named morning root, for a settled doom that overtakes people at daybreak. | terra: A settled punishment comes upon Lot's people بكرة, early in the morning, an especially direct instance of punishment arriving like the section's dawn raid.
terra: The opponents describe themselves as جميع منتصر, a united host able to prevail; this is precisely the confident human gathering into whose center the section's charge runs.
terra: سيهزم الجمع predicts that the gathered host of 54:44 will be defeated and turn its back, reversing the crowd's confidence at the moment of collision.
terra: After the worldly host's defeat in 54:44-45, the Hour is named their true appointment and something more calamitous and bitter; the battle rout explicitly becomes a prelude to final judgment.
terra: On the final day the crushed mountains become هباء منبثا, dispersed dust; the local dust cloud under hooves expands into the cosmic dust of the event the section says the raid rehearses.

luna: The people of the fortified houses think their strongholds will protect them, yet removal comes unexpectedly and terror is cast into their hearts; this is a specific reversal of the section's unprepared encampment, with confidence in defenses replacing sleep. | terra: The fortified people suppose their defenses will protect them, but judgment comes from where they do not reckon and terror enters their hearts; surprise and the failure of refuge enact the section's inescapable assault.
terra: The granted spoil is property for which the believers urged on neither horses nor camels; it directly reverses the section's mounted raid and its dictionary image of plunder awaiting division.

terra: The property following 59:6 is assigned among specified recipients so it does not circulate only among the rich; this ayah provides the principled distribution that replaces a raider's pre-division taking.

terra: The hostile groups appear جميعا while their hearts are شتى and fight from fortified places; it makes concrete the section's dictionary picture of a gathered yet mixed human crowd awaiting collision.

luna: The verse pairs “My enemy and your enemy” with taking them as allies (أَوْلِيَاءَ), directly staging the enemy/friend opposition noted in the source, in a concrete plot against the Messenger. | terra: The address لا تتخذوا عدوي وعدوكم أولياء places enemy and allies in the same prohibition, directly realizing the section's definition of عدو as the opposite of ولي.
luna: It says God may place affection between believers and those they currently oppose; this is a specific reversal of the enemy relation named in the section.

luna: God permits kindness and justice toward people who have not fought the believers or driven them from home; this limits the section's enemy/friend distinction by the actual conduct of the other party. | terra: Those who neither fight believers nor expel them may receive kindness and justice; it qualifies the enemy-ally vocabulary by refusing to turn mere difference into aggression.

luna: The next verse forbids taking as allies those who fought, expelled, or aided expulsion; it identifies the concrete hostile conduct that distinguishes an enemy from those addressed in 60:8. | terra: The prohibition on alliance is limited to those who fight, expel, and assist expulsion; this supplies the concrete hostile acts that distinguish an actual enemy from the peaceful people of 60:8.
terra: God gathers humanity ليوم الجمع and names that day the Day of Gathering; this is the eschatological destination of the section's physical جمع.
terra: When the threatened event is seen near, faces darken and they are told that this is what they used to demand; visual proximity turns provocation into panic.

luna: Garden owners swear to go early and harvest, but the overnight calamity in the surrounding passage ruins their plan; this is a specific dawn-going reversal of the section's successful dawn assault, though it is a harvest rather than combat.

luna: A calamity reaches the garden owners while they sleep, and 68:21–25 show them setting out early to find the loss; this is a dawn-vulnerability parallel, though it concerns a ruined orchard rather than an attacking force. | terra: A visitation from the Lord circles the garden وهم نائمون, while its owners sleep; this is the section's vulnerable camp overtaken before waking, with divine judgment as the assailant.
terra: By morning the garden has become كالصريم; following the seizure during sleep in 68:19, this ayah supplies the black, stripped dawn aftermath that the owners unexpectedly meet.

luna: The garden owners call to one another at daybreak after the nocturnal calamity of 68:19; the awakening-at-dawn timing parallels the raid's vulnerable hour, while the event is a crop's destruction rather than combat. | terra: The garden owners call one another مصبحين; within the passage where judgment struck during sleep, morning itself is marked by a collective call.
terra: They urge one another to go early to the crop if they mean to harvest; the ayah supplies a purposeful dawn departure that mirrors a raiding party's timed advance.

luna: They explicitly plan to keep a poor person out of the garden; this is a specific but indirect boundary on the source's booty-sharing detail, since the verse concerns hoarded produce rather than war spoils. | terra: Their whispered instruction is to let no poor person enter the garden that day; this row identifies the unjust exclusion motivating the early movement described around it.

luna: They set out early, confident and determined, only to find their garden ruined in 68:26; this reverses the section's confident mounted advance, but the connection is the dawn-discovered loss rather than a shared raid scene. | terra: The owners go out early على حرد قادرين, intent and confident, yet 68:19-20 show that the garden was already struck while they slept; the would-be dawn actors arrive as the surprised victims.

luna: One member described as the group's “middle” or most judicious person rebukes the others after their loss; the root w-s-ṭ shifts from the source's physical center of a crowd to a moral voice within a group. | terra: أوسطهم, the most balanced or best among the garden owners, recalls his ignored warning; within the same dawn-surprise passage, the section's physical و س ط becomes a moral middle voice inside the group.
terra: A single blast is blown in the trumpet; the emphatic one-time sound is the final-day counterpart of the raid's uninterrupted cry.
terra: A demander asks for a punishment that will fall; the request itself activates the section's answer that hastened punishment can descend like an attack.
terra: People emerge from the graves سراعا as though racing toward a marker; human beings now perform the headlong rush, but it carries them into judgment rather than into an enemy camp.
terra: The trumpet's sounding inaugurates a difficult day; it converts the section's raid-alarm into the signal of the final crisis.

luna: On the Day of Resurrection a person asks where escape is; this directly matches the section's claim that the charge into the crowd marks the moment with nowhere left to flee, and its explicit turn toward the final day. | terra: On that day the human being asks أين المفر, where escape is; it states the final-day meaning of the section's charge ending where no avenue of flight remains.

luna: The answer to the escape question in 75:10 is that there is no refuge; this verse supplies the inescapability that the section makes central to its dawn-strike image. | terra: كلا لا وزر answers the flight-question of 75:10 with “no refuge”; its own contribution is the categorical closure of every escape route.
terra: The trumpet is blown and people come in companies; it combines the final sound with human groups arriving together, directly joining the section's cry and جمع.
terra: Hell is described as مرصادا, a place lying in wait; it gives the final punishment an ambush structure that corresponds specifically to the section's surprise raid.
terra: The resurrection requires only one blast; the section's sustained alarm is reduced to a single decisive eschatological sound.
terra: Following the one blast of 79:13, everyone is suddenly on the open surface; this row supplies the immediate mass appearance caused by that sound.
terra: After recalling destroyed tyrants, the surah says إن ربك لبالمرصاد; the Lord's watch or ambush position makes hidden judgment answer the attackers who assume the initiative.
